name: 15g temperature reshaping
title: Temperature reshapes one distribution without changing its order
subtitle: Prompt "My coffee is too"; logits 3.0, 2.5, 2.0, 1.5, 1.0, 0.0; probability = exp(logit / T) / sum

steps.caption: At T = 1 the model's own probabilities are used. Each logit is exponentiated and divided by the sum of all six exponentials, so hot gets 20.09 / 47.86 = 0.420.
Lowering the temperature to 0.85 multiplies every logit by 1 / T, which stretches the gaps between them.
Lowering the temperature to 0.7 multiplies every logit by 1 / T, which stretches the gaps between them.
Lowering the temperature to 0.6 multiplies every logit by 1 / T, which stretches the gaps between them.
At T = 0.5 every logit doubles, so the gap between hot and strong grows from 0.5 to 1.0. Hot rises to 0.635 and loud falls from 0.021 to 0.002. The ranking never changes.
Raising the temperature to 0.75 divides every logit by more than 1 and squeezes the gaps together.
Raising the temperature to 1 divides every logit by more than 1 and squeezes the gaps together.
Raising the temperature to 1.3 divides every logit by more than 1 and squeezes the gaps together.
Raising the temperature to 1.65 divides every logit by more than 1 and squeezes the gaps together.
At T = 2 every logit halves, so hot falls to 0.290 and loud rises to 0.065, about three times its T = 1 share. Unlikely words now get drawn noticeably more often.
As T approaches 0 the largest logit wins every draw, so sampling becomes greedy decoding. Most APIs treat T = 0 as a request for the argmax rather than dividing by zero.
